papers.title: Mutation is all you need
papers.abstract: Neural architecture search (NAS) promises to make deep learning accessible to non-experts by automating architecture engineering of deep neural networks. BANANAS is one state-of-the-art NAS method that is embedded within the Bayesian optimization framework. Recent experimental findings have demonstrated the strong performance of BANANAS on the NAS-Bench-101 benchmark being determined by its path encoding and not its choice of surrogate model. We present experimental results suggesting that the performance of BANANAS on the NAS-Bench-301 benchmark is determined by its acquisition function optimizer, which minimally mutates the incumbent.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关于神经网络架构搜索，与有限元代理模型或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on neural architecture search for deep learning models, not on surrogate modeling for expensive physical simulations, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or implant/biomechanics design.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究BANANAS神经网络架构搜索方法性能的决定因素
summary_zh.method: 通过实验分析路径编码和采集函数优化器对性能的影响
summary_zh.result: 发现性能主要由采集函数优化器决定而非代理模型

summary_en.motivation: Investigate the key factors driving the performance of the BANANAS neural architecture search method.
summary_en.method: Perform ablation experiments to isolate the contributions of path encoding and acquisition function optimizer.
summary_en.result: Show that the performance is primarily determined by the acquisition function optimizer, not the surrogate model or path encoding.
summary_en.validation: Validate on the NAS-Bench-301 benchmark dataset.

papers.title: Multiple-criteria Based Active Learning with Fixed-size Determinantal Point Processes
papers.abstract: Active learning aims to achieve greater accuracy with less training data by selecting the most useful data samples from which it learns. Single-criterion based methods (i.e., informativeness and representativeness based methods) are simple and efficient; however, they lack adaptability to different real-world scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a multiple-criteria based active learning algorithm, which incorporates three complementary criteria, i.e., informativeness, representativeness and diversity, to make appropriate selections in the active learning rounds under different data types. We consider the selection process as a Determinantal Point Process, which good balance among these criteria. We refine the query selection strategy by both selecting the hardest unlabeled data sample and biasing towards the classifiers that are more suitable for the current data distribution. In addition, we also consider the dependencies and relationships between these data points in data selection by means of centroidbased clustering approaches. Through evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, we show that our method performs significantly better and is more stable than other multiple-criteria based AL algorithms.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文提出的多准则主动学习方法可潜在用于代理模型的训练数据筛选，但未涉及有限元分析、约束处理或不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA simulation, no surrogate modeling for expensive sampling, no constraint handling, and no UQ or implant/biomechanics context.

summary_zh.motivation: 为解决主动学习中单一准则适应性不足的问题
summary_zh.method: 提出结合信息性、代表性和多样性的多准则主动学习算法，采用行列式点过程平衡准则
summary_zh.result: 在合成和真实数据集上表现优于其他多准则方法且更稳定
summary_zh.validation: 在分类/回归数据集上进行了实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To overcome the lack of adaptability of single-criterion active learning methods to diverse real-world scenarios.
summary_en.method: Proposes a multiple-criteria active learning algorithm that balances informativeness, representativeness, and diversity using Determinantal Point Processes and clustering.
summary_en.result: Achieves significantly better and more stable performance than other multiple-criteria active learning methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.
summary_en.validation: Validated on standard classification and regression benchmark datasets, not on engineering simulations.

papers.title: Deep Gaussian Process Emulation using Stochastic Imputation
papers.abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) provide a rich class of models that can better represent functions with varying regimes or sharp changes, compared to conventional GPs. In this work, we propose a novel inference method for DGPs for computer model emulation. By stochastically imputing the latent layers, our approach transforms a DGP into a linked GP: a novel emulator developed for systems of linked computer models. This transformation permits an efficient DGP training procedure that only involves optimizations of conventional GPs. In addition, predictions from DGP emulators can be made in a fast and analytically tractable manner by naturally utilizing the closed form predictive means and variances of linked GP emulators. We demonstrate the method in a series of synthetic examples and empirical applications, and show that it is a competitive candidate for DGP surrogate inference, combining efficiency that is comparable to doubly stochastic variational inference and uncertainty quantification that is comparable to the fully-Bayesian approach. A $\texttt{Python}$ package $\texttt{dgpsi}$ implementing the method is also produced and available at https://github.com/mingdeyu/DGP.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法提出了一种新的深度高斯过程推理方法，可迁移用于构建有限元代理模型，提高昂贵仿真采样效率并提供不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not apply the method to FEA surrogate modeling or biomechanics constraints, nor does it handle optimization constraints; it focuses solely on methodological development for DGP inference.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高深度高斯过程在计算机模型仿真中的推断效率
summary_zh.method: 通过随机插补隐层将DGP转化为链接GP进行训练
summary_zh.result: 预测准确且不确定性量化良好，效率接近变分推断
summary_zh.validation: 合成数据和经验应用验证

summary_en.motivation: To improve inference efficiency for deep Gaussian process (DGP) emulators.
summary_en.method: Transform a DGP into a linked GP by stochastically imputing latent layers, enabling efficient training and tractable predictions.
summary_en.result: The method provides competitive uncertainty quantification while maintaining efficiency comparable to variational inference.
summary_en.validation: Demonstrated on synthetic examples and empirical applications.
